+* **Mermaid interop** — imports mermaid `flowchart` and C4 diagrams via converter;
+  exports to mermaid with declared feature drop. The native grammar is its own —
+  *inspired by* mermaid, not bound to its syntax.
+* **Flows & animation** — IcePanel-style step-by-step flow playback (8 step types) over
+  static diagrams.
+* **Workspace** — multiple files, directory tree, per-file import/export, full ZIP
+  export/import.
+* **Zero server storage** — everything lives in the browser; nothing is sent anywhere.
+* **Shipable two ways** — fully static on GitHub Pages, *and* as a single Go binary
+  (Windows/Linux/macOS) that serves the app plus a headless CLI (`validate` / `convert`
+  / `render`).
+
+### Out of scope (explicitly)
+
+Real-time collaboration, authentication, server-side persistence, AI assistance, mobile
+native apps. Full mermaid feature coverage (only the subset in [FILE-FORMAT.md](FILE-FORMAT.md)).
+
+---
+
+## 2. Decisions locked with product owner
+
+| # | Decision | Choice |
+|---|----------|--------|
+| D1 | Model topology | **Hybrid**: files are standalone diagrams; objects may reference other files via `imports` (link-style reuse) |
+| D2 | Rendering | **Custom SVG engine**; mermaid.js is *never* the editor renderer — mermaid is import/export text format only |
+| D3 | Go binary role | Static app server **+ headless CLI** (`validate`, `convert`, `render` via headless Chrome) |
+| D4 | Frontend stack | **Preact** for UI chrome + framework-agnostic TypeScript SVG engine |
+| D5 | Flows | **All 8 IcePanel step types in v1** (see §7) |
+| D6 | Quality gates | Go: `staticcheck` + `gocyclo`; JS: `eslint` (incl. complexity rules) + `vitest`, **≥80% coverage on core packages**; E2E: **Playwright + vision review in dev loop** |
+| D7 | Native file format | Own `.pcd` grammar, mermaid-**inspired**; **no mermaid-validity requirement**. Mermaid handled by import converter and lossy exporter only |
+| D8 | License | **GPL-3.0-only** (SPDX `GPL-3.0-only`), LICENSE file at repo root |
+
+Rationale for each: ADR 0001–0005.
+
+---
+
+## 3. Users & key scenarios
+
+**Persona A — Architect (author).** Maintains a workspace of diagrams describing a
+system landscape. Creates diagrams visually, refines them in code view, animates flows
+to explain request journeys.
+
+**Persona B — Reviewer (reader).** Opens a shared `.pcd` file or ZIP, walks flows in
+play mode, exports PNG/SVG for docs.
+
+**Top scenarios (must work end-to-end):**
+
+1. *S1 Create*: new file → drag person/system/container onto canvas → link them → set
+   properties → diagram renders live; code view shows updated source.
+2. *S2 Code round-trip*: paste a mermaid `C4Container` snippet into code view → canvas
+   renders it → edit node in canvas → code view updates; file remains valid mermaid
+   (PanelCraft extensions live in comment block).
+3. *S3 Flow playback*: define 6-step flow (incl. one `alt`, one `par`) → press Play →
+   camera focus + animated edges step-by-step; non-active elements dim.
+4. *S4 Workspace IO*: build directory tree `landscape/`, `systems/billing/` → export ZIP →
+   clear browser data → import ZIP → identical workspace.
+5. *S5 Mermaid import*: open `architecture.mmd` (flowchart + subgraphs) → converted to
+   `.pcd`, auto-laid-out, fully editable.
+6. *S6 CLI*: `panelcraft validate ./diagrams` lints all files (CI gate);
+   `panelcraft render checkout.pcd --out checkout.png` produces a PNG via headless Chrome.
+7. *S7 Static hosting*: open the GitHub Pages URL → full functionality offline-capable,
+   no backend calls (verified by network monitor in E2E).
+
+---
+
+## 4. Functional requirements
+
+### 4.1 Workspace & files (FR-W)
+
+* **FR-W1** Virtual file tree with folders and `.pcd` files; create, rename, delete,
+  move (drag & drop), duplicate.
+* **FR-W2** Multi-tab editing; unsaved-changes indicator; autosave (see FR-S1).
+* **FR-W3** Per-file import: `.pcd`, `.mmd`/`.mermaid` (mermaid text), `.txt` (treated as mermaid).
+* **FR-W4** Per-file export: `.pcd`, `.mmd` (mermaid subset export), `.svg`, `.png`
+  (current view), `.seq.mmd` (flows exported as mermaid `sequenceDiagram`, optional M6).
+* **FR-W5** Workspace ZIP export (`workspace.zip`, plain folder layout + optional
+  `panelcraft.workspace.json` manifest) and ZIP import; round-trip must be lossless.
+* **FR-W6** Global quick search (`Ctrl/Cmd+P`): files, objects, flows (M6).
+* **FR-W7** Snapshots: manual named snapshots of the whole workspace, restore point
+  (M6, local only).
+
+### 4.2 Canvas editor (FR-C)
+
+* **FR-C1** Pan (space-drag / wheel-drag / trackpad), zoom (wheel/pinch, 10%–400%),
+  fit-to-selection, fit-to-diagram, zoom controls, mini-map (M6).
+* **FR-C2** Grid + snap-to-grid (toggleable); alignment guides when dragging.
+* **FR-C3** Stencil palette (C4 types): Person, Software System, External System,
+  Container, Component, Data Store, Queue/Topic, Group/Boundary, Note.
+  Drag-drop or click-to-place.
+* **FR-C4** Objects: select, multi-select (rubber band, shift-click), drag, resize
+  (groups/boundaries), rotate *not* supported (C4 shapes are axis-aligned).
+* **FR-C5** Inline rename (double-click), description tooltip, icon per object
+  (built-in icon set, M5).
+* **FR-C6** Properties panel: name, description, technology, tags (multi),
+  custom key-value properties, style overrides (fill, border, text color, icon).
+* **FR-C7** Connections: drag from port/edge halo to target; typed links
+  (`uses`, `includes`, `requests`, `returns`, `publishes`, `subscribes`, `reads`,
+  `writes`, `data`, custom); label; direction (uni/bi); arrowhead styles; dashed/solid.
+* **FR-C8** Edge routing: orthogonal (default), curved (bezier), straight; drag
+  waypoints; per-edge style override.
+* **FR-C9** Undo/redo (command stack, coalesced typing/drag operations, ≥100 steps),
+  full keyboard shortcuts (§10).
+* **FR-C10** Context menus: canvas, object, edge (duplicate, delete, bring-to-front,
+  add to group, create flow step from link…).
+* **FR-C11** Dependencies view of selected object: highlight incoming/outgoing + list
+  panel (M6).
+* **FR-C12** Copy/paste/duplicate objects within and across files (internal clipboard;
+  cross-file paste resolves missing imports by inlining).
+
+### 4.3 Code view (FR-K)
+
+* **FR-K1** Split layout: canvas + code side-by-side (horizontal or vertical), or
+  single-pane toggle. CodeMirror-based editor (see ADR-0004) with PanelCraft syntax
+  highlighting.
+* **FR-K2** Live two-way sync, debounced (canvas → code ≤150 ms; code → canvas on
+  idle/pause or explicit apply if parse errors).
+* **FR-K3** Diagnostics: parse/validation errors shown inline (line:col) + problem
+  panel; error state never loses user text.
+* **FR-K4** Format-on-save (canonical pretty-printer, idempotent).
+* **FR-K5** The saved file is the **source of truth**; canvas state is a projection.
+  Closing a file with diverged editor buffer prompts to apply/discard.
+
+### 4.4 Mermaid interop (FR-M) — details in FILE-FORMAT.md
+
+* **FR-M1** Import converter, mermaid `flowchart`/`graph` (incl. subgraphs, edge labels,
+  shapes) → PDL, with shape→semantic-type mapping (documented table) and auto-layout.
+* **FR-M2** Import converter, mermaid C4 (`C4Context`, `C4Container`, `C4Component`,
+  `C4Dynamic` incl. `System*`, `Container*`, `Rel*`, `Deployment*` subset) → PDL
+  objects/links; `Show*`/layout directives ignored.
+* **FR-M3** Import converter, mermaid `sequenceDiagram` → optional conversion to a Flow
+  over participant boxes (M6).
+* **FR-M4** Export to mermaid (`flowchart`): nodes, typed edges, labels, subgroups;
+  **feature drop is declared and documented** — flows/animations, manual positions
+  (replaced by auto-layout), styles (approximated by mermaid classes), properties,
+  imports are not representable. Export is one-way; PDL remains the only source of truth.
+* **FR-M5** Import diagnostics: unsupported mermaid constructs reported with line:col;
+  conversion never silently drops content. Export fidelity matrix documented (FR-M4).
+* **FR-M6** No mermaid-validity requirement on `.pcd` files; mermaid compatibility is
+  converter-only, in both directions.
+
+### 4.5 Flows & animation (FR-F)
+
+IcePanel-style visual storytelling over the static diagram.
+
+* **FR-F1** Multiple named flows per diagram; flow editor: ordered step list, drag to
+  reorder, per-step title + description.
+* **FR-F2** Step types (all in v1):
+  | Type | Meaning | Visual behavior |
+  |---|---|---|
+  | `intro` | Set the scene | Show all steps overview; no dimming |
+  | `msg` | Message A→B over existing link (direction may be flipped for the step) | Animated moving token along edge, step number badge, focus both ends |
+  | `process` | Single object does something | Pulse/emphasis on object + badge |
+  | `alt` | OR branches | Branch selector UI; plays chosen path; others dimmed |
+  | `par` | AND parallel | Steps animate concurrently on split lanes |
+  | `goto` | Jump to another flow (same or other file), optional return point | Navigate; breadcrumb to return |
+  | `info` | Free text not tied to elements | Info toast/card |
+  | `conclusion` | Close story | Show summary; un-dim |
+* **FR-F3** Play mode: play/pause/step-forward/step-back/restart, per-step auto delay
+  (default 2.5 s, configurable per step), exit restores pre-play view state.
+* **FR-F4** Animation style: edge token (circle) traveling with trailing dash animation,
+  object emphasis ring, non-participants dimmed to 25% opacity, smooth camera
+  (pan/zoom to step actors, 300 ms ease). All timing constants in theme config.
+* **FR-F5** Reduced-motion: respect `prefers-reduced-motion` → crossfade instead of
+  movement.
+* **FR-F6** Flow validation: steps reference existing objects/links; dangling refs are
+  errors (code view + validate CLI).
+
+### 4.6 Views, tags, layout (FR-V)
+
+* **FR-V1** Tags on objects/links; tag filter bar → fade non-matching (perspectives).
+* **FR-V2** Named views per diagram: element visibility set, tag filters, saved
+  positions, layout mode (`auto:LR|TB` or `saved`). Diagram has ≥1 view; default view
+  implicit.
+* **FR-V3** Auto-layout: layered (direction LR/TB) via dagre behind a `LayoutEngine`
+  port; deterministic for identical input (stable ordering by id).
+* **FR-V4** Manual positions stored in file; mixing auto + pinned nodes supported.
+
+### 4.7 Imports & reuse (FR-I) — hybrid model (D1)
+
+* **FR-I1** `imports:` section maps aliases → relative file paths; imported file's
+  *objects* are referenceable (ghost rendering: dashed border, "imported" badge).
+* **FR-I2** Imported objects are read-only in the importing file; click-through opens
+  source file (workspace-relative).
+* **FR-I3** Cycle detection: import graph must be acyclic (error otherwise).
+* **FR-I4** Missing import file → explicit problem marker, diagram still renders
+  non-imported content.
+
+### 4.8 Storage (FR-S)
+
+* **FR-S1** Persistence: IndexedDB autosave, debounced 800 ms; last-open workspace
+  restored on load. Storage model = **browser-local only**; "nothing server-side" is a
+  hard constraint (E2E asserts zero network calls after initial load).
+* **FR-S2** Ephemeral mode ("private tab" toggle): in-memory only, no IDB writes;
+  export reminder banner every 10 min.
+* **FR-S3** Quota handling: surface quota errors; graceful degradation to ephemeral
+  mode with warning; storage usage indicator in settings.
+* **FR-S4** Reset/clear-all-data with typed confirmation.
+* **FR-S5** Schema versioning of stored workspace (migrations forward-only).
+
+### 4.9 CLI (Go binary) (FR-X)
+
+Single static binary, no runtime deps, all assets embedded (`go:embed`).
+
+* `panelcraft serve [--addr :8080] [--open] [dir]` — serves the SPA at `/`, workspace
+  files under `[dir]` read-only at `/files/*` (optional convenience for demo assets).
+  SPA fallback to `index.html`. No write endpoints, ever.
+* `panelcraft validate <file|dir>... [--json]` — parse + semantic validation
+  (dangling refs, import cycles, flow refs, duplicate ids). Exit 0 clean; exit 1
+  findings; exit 2 usage/IO error. CI-friendly.
+* `panelcraft convert <in.mmd> [-o out.pcd]` — mermaid → PanelCraft canonical form.
+* `panelcraft render <file.pcd> --out out.png|svg [--width 1920] [--theme dark|light]
+  [--view NAME] [--chrome /path/to/chrome]` — headless render via Chrome DevTools
+  Protocol (chromedp, pure Go). Serve embedded app, drive it, screenshot/serialize SVG.
+  Fails with actionable error if no Chrome found.
+* `panelcraft version`.
+
+### 4.10 Hosting (FR-H)
+
+* **FR-H1** GitHub Pages deployment of the built SPA on `main` (Actions). App runs
+  100% static; base-path configurable at build time (`/panelcraft/`).
+* **FR-H2** GitHub Releases attach binaries: `panelcraft_{linux,darwin,windows}_{amd64,arm64}`
+  (+ checksums). Windows = `.zip`, others `.tar.gz`.
+
+---
+
+## 5. Non-functional requirements
+
+| ID | Requirement | Target |
+|----|-------------|--------|
+| N1 | Render/interaction perf | 60 fps pan/zoom & drag ≤300 objects; ≤2 000 objects usable (layer virtualization) |
+| N2 | Open time | 100-object file → interactive < 300 ms (mid-range laptop) |
+| N3 | Parser perf | 10k-line file parses < 1 s |
+| N4 | Binary size | < 30 MB compressed |
+| N5 | Accessibility | WCAG 2.1 AA for UI chrome; canvas: full keyboard object nav, ARIA live narration in play mode; `prefers-reduced-motion` honored |
+| N6 | Security | Strict CSP (no inline script eval in app), exported SVG sanitized (no scripts/foreignObject from untrusted labels), CLI: path traversal guarded, no telemetry |
+| N7 | Privacy | Zero network calls at runtime (self-hosted fonts or system font stack); verifiable in E2E |
+| N8 | Offline | App shell + last workspace available offline (service worker, M7) |
+| N9 | Browser support | Evergreen Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Safari (last 2 versions); `CompressionStream` required (Safari ≥16.4), fallback dependency fflate if feature absent (ADR-0004) |
+| N10 | i18n | English v1; all strings centralized for later l10n |
+
+### Visual style targets (validated by vision review, §9)
+
+* Dark-first theme, high contrast, C4-ish shape language (soft rectangles, person
+  glyph), consistent 4 px spacing grid, subtle shadows, 150–300 ms transitions.
+* Style guide + golden screenshots per milestone (docs/STYLE-GUIDE.md in M0).
+
+---
+
+## 6. File format (summary — full spec in FILE-FORMAT.md)
+
+* Native format **PDL (PanelCraft Diagram Language)**, extension `.pcd`, UTF-8,
+  **own grammar inspired by mermaid** — deliberately *not* required to be valid mermaid
+  (D7). One coherent syntax for structure *and* semantics: typed nodes, typed links,
+  plus first-class `flow`, `view`, `import`, `style`, `tag` directives — no comment-block
+  workarounds.
+* Mermaid enters/leaves the tool exclusively through converters:
+  * import: mermaid → PDL (lossless for supported subset, diagnostics otherwise);
+  * export: PDL → mermaid (lossy, declared feature drop).
+* Guarantees:
+  * PDL ⇄ internal IR ⇄ PDL is lossless (canonical round-trip, golden-tested).
+  * Parser accepts unknown-but-parseable constructs as data (forward compatibility),
+    reports them as warnings; semantic validation is a separate pass.
+* Internal **IR = language-neutral JSON schema** — shared contract between the TS
+  implementation and the Go CLI (parser parity tests, §8).
+
+---
+
+## 7. Domain model (IR overview)
+
+```
+Workspace { schemaVersion, files[], settings }
+File      { path, meta, imports[], objects[], links[], groups[], flows[], views[] }
+Object    { id, kind(person|system|system_ext|container|component|datastore|queue|group|note),
+            name, description, technology, tags[], properties{}, style{}, importedFrom? }
+Link      { id, from, to, type, label, direction(uni|bi), style{}, waypoints[] }
+Flow      { id, title, description?, steps[] }
+Step      { id, type(intro|msg|process|alt|par|goto|info|conclusion), title?, description?,
+            payload (per type: from/to/linkRef | on | branches[](label,steps[]) | branches[](steps[]) |
+                     target{file?,flow,return} | text) }
+View      { id, name, layout(auto:LR|auto:TB|saved), positions{}, hiddenTags?, elements? }
+```
+
+Rules: ids are stable strings (`[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, unique per file); link endpoints must
+resolve to objects or imported aliases; flows reference link ids for `msg` steps
+(mermaid-imported edges get auto ids `L1..Ln` recorded in `links:` so flows survive
+round-trips).
+
+---
+
+## 8. Quality strategy (gates, per D6)
+
+### 8.1 Static analysis & complexity
+
+* **Go**: `go vet`, `staticcheck` (default checks, zero findings), `gocyclo` —
+  **target ≤10, hard fail >15** per function; `gocognit` ≤30. Enforced in CI on
+  `./...`.
+* **TypeScript**: `eslint` — `complexity ≤12`, `max-lines-per-function ≤120`,
+  `max-depth ≤4`, `@typescript-eslint` strict; `tsc --noEmit` clean. Same thresholds
+  in CI. Deliberate exceptions require `// rationale:` comment + ADR note.
+
+### 8.2 Unit tests (vitest / go test) — coverage plan
+
+Core packages (**≥80% lines+branches, enforced by vitest thresholds**):
+
+| Package (TS) | Must cover |
+|---|---|
+| `engine/format` | PDL parser/printer: golden corpus round-trips (see below), error positions, mermaid import mapping incl. malformed input |
+| `engine/model` | IR ops: add/remove/update object/link/flow, import resolution, cycle detection, validation rules |
+| `engine/layout` | dagre adapter: determinism, pin handling |
+| `engine/render` | scene-graph → SVG snapshot assertions (jsdom), element hit lists |
+| `engine/flows` | step machine: all 8 types, alt/par branching, goto resolution, timing plan |
+| `engine/anim` | animation plan builder (durations/keyframes), reduced-motion path |
+| `workspace/store` | virtual FS ops, ZIP pack/unpack (round-trip), IDB wrapper (via `fake-indexeddb`), migrations |
+| `workspace/undo` | command stack, coalescing |
+| `ui/*` | component tests (@testing-library/preact): panels, palette, dialogs (**≥60%, reported, not gated**) |
+
+Go: table-driven tests for `validate`/`convert`/IR codec; `httptest` for server;
+corpus parity tests below.
+
+**Golden corpus**: `testdata/corpus/` — ≥30 curated files (mermaid samples, C4
+samples, flows incl. alt/par/goto, edge cases: unicode, long labels, deep nesting,
+malformed variants). Each file has expected `.ir.json` + canonical `.pcd`. Shared by
+TS and Go tests → **parser parity is a CI gate** (IR diff must be empty).
+
+### 8.3 E2E (Playwright)
+
+* Scenarios map 1:1 to §3 scenarios S1–S7 plus: undo/redo, tag filtering, theme
+  switch, zip round-trip, quota-error path (mocked), keyboard-only editing pass.
+* **No-network assertion** (S7): route-block all external requests; app must function.
+* Screenshots at every scenario end (light+dark) → committed baselines for visual diff
+  (pixelmatch, 0.1 threshold) and as input for vision review.
+
+### 8.4 Vision validation loop (development-time)
+
+Each milestone: run E2E suite → collect screenshots → agent reviews them against
+docs/STYLE-GUIDE.md checklist (alignment, contrast, spacing, animation end-states) →
+file UI defects with screenshot refs → fix → re-shoot. Vision review is a **definition-
+of-done item per milestone**, recorded in the milestone log. (Playwright visual diff is
+the CI regression net; vision review catches *quality* issues diffing can't.)
+
+### 8.5 CI (GitHub Actions)
+
+* `ci.yml`: lint+staticcheck+gocyclo → unit tests (Go matrix + Node) → coverage gate
+  → corpus parity → build web → e2e (Playwright, chromium) → visual diff.
+* `release.yml`: tag → cross-compile binaries (matrix GOOS/GOARCH, CGO off) →
+  checksums → GitHub Release.
+* `pages.yml`: deploy built SPA to GitHub Pages on main.
+
+---
+
+## 9. Milestones
+
+| M | Scope | Done means |
+|---|-------|-----------|
+| M0 | Scaffolding: repo, CI, vite+preact+ts setup, agents.md, STYLE-GUIDE, empty app served by Go bin | CI green end-to-end; S7 skeleton passes |
+| M1 | Format engine: IR schema, PDL parser/printer, mermaid import, golden corpus, Go parser parity, `validate`/`convert` CLI | Corpus green both sides; FR-M1/M2 import tests |
+| M2 | Canvas MVP: render engine, pan/zoom, select/drag, palette drop, linking, properties panel, undo | S1 passes E2E + vision review |
+| M3 | Workspace: file tree, tabs, IDB storage, zip, per-file IO | S4 passes; FR-W* |
+| M4 | Code view sync + mermaid export + format-on-save + diagnostics | S2 passes; FR-K*, FR-M4 |
+| M5 | Flows + animation + icons + themes | S3 passes; FR-F* |
+| M6 | Tags/views, auto-layout, dependencies view, search, snapshots, seq export | FR-V*, FR-W6/W7 |
+| M7 | A11y pass, perf pass (N1–N3), service worker, docs complete, release engineering, GH Pages live | All NFRs measured; v1.0 released |
+
+---
+
+## 10. Keyboard shortcuts (v1 baseline)
+
+`Ctrl/Cmd+S` save+format · `Ctrl/Cmd+Z / Shift+Z` undo/redo · `Ctrl/Cmd+E` play/edit
+toggle · `Ctrl/Cmd+P` quick search · `Ctrl/Cmd+K` command palette (M6) · `Tab/Shift+Tab`
+cycle objects · arrows nudge (grid step; `Shift` = 1 px) · `Enter` properties ·
+`Ctrl/Cmd+D` duplicate · `Del` delete · `1..9` palette quick-add · `L` then click
+target = link mode · `F` fit · `+/-/0` zoom in/out/reset.
+
+---
+
+## 11. Risks & mitigations
+
+| Risk | Mitigation |
+|---|---|
+| TS/Go parser drift | Single IR JSON contract + shared golden corpus, parity CI gate (§8.2) |
+| SVG perf on large diagrams | Layer virtualization, offscreen culling, perf test in E2E (N1) budget; document limits |
+| ZIP without deps breaks on older Safari | Feature-detect `CompressionStream`; fflate fallback (ADR-0004) |
+| Mermaid subset mismatch (user pastes unsupported syntax) | Import converter diagnostics with line numbers + documented fidelity matrix (FR-M4/M5); never silent data loss |
+| Headless render env differences | chromedp pinned; CI runs `render` smoke test on linux; documented `--chrome` flag |
+| Scope creep (IcePanel parity temptation) | Milestone table is the contract; new ideas → backlog, not current milestone |
+| IndexedDB data loss (user clears browser) | Autosave + export reminders + zip (S4); quota/ephemeral handling FR-S2/S3 |
+
+---
+
+## 12. Open items (post-v1 backlog)
+
+Comments/annotations on objects · export to draw.io/PlantUML · plugin API for custom
+stencils · additional diagram notations (sequence-native, deployment advanced) ·
+optional file-system access API for real folders.
+
+---
+
+## 13. License
+
+* **GPL-3.0-only** (SPDX: `GPL-3.0-only`). `LICENSE` (full text) at repo root; each
+  source file carries the standard GPL header; SPDX headers in every source file.
+* Binary distribution (GitHub Releases) satisfies GPL-3.0 corresponding-source by
+  linking the public repository + commit reference in release notes.
+* Third-party dependencies must be GPL-compatible (MIT / Apache-2.0 / BSD). New
+  dependencies require a license check recorded in the ADR proposing them.
+* Documentation and sample diagrams in-repo: same license, CC-BY-SA-4.0 acceptable
+  alternative for docs/ only — decision recorded in ADR-0005.

{"content":"# PanelCraft Diagram Language (PDL) — File Format Specification

**Extension:** `.pcd` · **Encoding:** UTF-8 (no BOM) · **Format version:** `pcd/1`
**Status:** Draft v1 (implemented in M1) · **License:** GPL-3.0-only

PDL is PanelCraft's native text format. It is **line-oriented and mermaid-inspired**
(arrow-based links, `id` + `Label` node syntax) but is an **independent grammar**:
mermaid validity is *not* a goal (SPEC D7). Mermaid enters/leaves only via converters
(§8, §9). PDL is the single source of truth; the canvas is a projection of it.

Design goals, in order:

1. **Human-writable in code view** — a diagram readable top-to-bottom like source code.
2. **Lossless round-trip** — `PDL → IR → PDL` is byte-stable after canonical formatting.
3. **Forward compatible** — unknown-but-parseable constructs survive round-trips as data.
4. **Deterministic printing** — canonical printer output is stable (golden-tested, diffable).

---

## 1. Lexical rules

* Lines are the primary unit; blocks group lines with `{ … }`.
* Comments: `#` to end of line. Inside quoted strings `#` has no special meaning.
* Strings: double-quoted `"…"`; escapes `\"` and `\\`; unquoted *words* allowed where a
  single token suffices (`technology Go`), but the canonical printer always emits quotes.
* Identifiers (ids, aliases, tag names): `[a-z][a-z0-9_-]*`, case-sensitive, max 64 chars.
* Whitespace: leading indentation is **stylistic only** (blocks are brace-scoped) — the
  parser never infers structure from indentation.
* Line endings: `\n` (canonical); parser accepts `\r\n`.
* Max line length: none enforced; printer wraps labels > 100 chars only in views? **No —
  printer never wraps content** (stability over prettiness).

## 2. File structure

A file is an **ordered sequence of top-level statements**. Canonical order (printer
output; parser accepts any order, diagnostics for duplicates):

```
pcd 1.0                      ← REQUIRED, first non-comment line ("magic")
title "Checkout"             ← optional meta (0..n meta directives)
level container              ← context | container | component | deployment
direction LR                 ← auto-layout hint: LR | TB | RL | BT
theme dark                   ← light | dark (render hint only)

import billing as "../billing/system.pcd"    ← 0..n, see §5

<objects>                    ← 0..n, see §3
<links>                      ← 0..n, see §4
<flows>                      ← 0..n, see §6
<views>                      ← 0..n, see §7
<style-overrides>            ← 0..n, see §7.3
```

`pcd 1.0` — if absent or major version > implementation's, the file is rejected with a
version diagnostic (never silently mis-parsed).

## 3. Objects

```
ObjectStmt  := Kind Id [QuotedName] [Block]
Kind        := person | system | system_ext | container | component
             | datastore | queue | group | note
Block       := "{" Line* "}"
```

* `QuotedName` defaults to the id if omitted (printer always emits it).
* Block body — attribute statements, each at most once (duplicates = error):

```
description "…"
technology "…"
tag t1 t2 …                 ← repeatable; merges
property key "value"        ← repeatable; custom key-value (key = identifier)
contains id1 id2 …          ← group only: membership (membership is *only* set here,
                              i.e. an object never names its group)
attach id                   ← note only: anchored object id
icon name                   ← built-in icon id (M5)
```

* `group` renders as boundary rectangle around `contains` members (C4 boundary).
* `note` renders as sticky annotation; `attach` is optional (free-floating otherwise).

Example:

```
pcd 1.0
title "Checkout"
level container

person user "Shopper"
system shop "Webshop" {
  description "Storefront SPA"
  technology "React"
  tag core shop
  property owner "team-commerce"
}
system_ext erp "Legacy ERP"
container api "Checkout API" { technology "Go" tag core pci }
datastore db "Orders DB" { technology "PostgreSQL" }
queue events "order.events" { technology "Kafka" }
group ctx "Checkout context" { contains api db }
note n1 "PCI scope ends at PSP" { attach erp }
```

## 4. Links

```
LinkStmt    := Id ArrowTail [Type] ArrowHead Id [":" QuotedLabel] ["as" Id]
ArrowTail   := "-"          | "<-"
ArrowHead   := "->"         | "->"   (with head "<-" ⇒ direction flags)
Type        := "-" Ident "-"            e.g. -requests-  (default: uses)
Direction   := "a -> b" uni a→b · "a <- b" uni b→a · "a <-> b" bidirectional
```

Grammar (single coherent form, no mermaid alias soup):

```
a -type-> b : "label" as L1     typed, labeled, named
a -> b                          default type `uses`
a <- b : "polled by"            reversed direction
a <-> b                         bidirectional
```

* **Link ids**: optional via `as L1`. Auto-assigned at import/canvas-create as `L<n>`
  (first free number). Printer emits explicit ids **only when referenced** by a flow
  step (minimal noise) or when non-default type/style demands clarity — deterministic
  rule, golden-tested.
* **Multiple links between same pair**: allowed, distinguished by id.
* Link endpoints must resolve to objects or imported aliases (§5) — semantic validation.
* Block form for link attributes (rare; printer uses it only when needed):

```
api -publishes-> events as L7 {
  label "order created v2"
  style { dashed }
  waypoint (120, 300)         ← 0..n, canvas routing hints, view-independent
}
```

## 5. Imports (hybrid reuse, SPEC D1)

```
import Alias as "./relative/path.pcd"
```

* Path: workspace-relative, POSIX separators, must stay inside workspace (`..` may not
  escape root — traversal error).
* The imported file's top-level **objects become referenceable** as `Alias.objectId`.
* Imported objects render ghosted (dashed border, "imported" badge); read-only; link
  endpoints may reference them; flows may include them.
* Import graph must be **acyclic**; missing files are warnings with problem markers,
  not parse errors (diagram still renders).
* What is *not* imported: flows, views, styles, links of the imported file (links always
  live in the file that draws them).

## 6. Flows

```
FlowStmt    := "flow" [QuotedName] ["as" Id] "{" Step* "}"
```

Steps (ordered; each becomes one numbered beat in playback):

```
Step        := IntroStep | MsgStep | ProcessStep | AltStep | ParStep
             | GotoStep | InfoStep | ConclusionStep

IntroStep       := "intro" QuotedText
MsgStep         := Id LinkTail [Type] LinkHead Id [":" QuotedLabel] ["as" RefId] ["flip"]
                   // resolves to an existing link between the pair (see below)
ProcessStep     := "process" Id [QuotedText]
AltStep         := "alt" [QuotedText] "{" (Branch)* "}"
Branch          := QuotedText "{" Step* "}"          // branch label + its steps
ParStep         := "par" [QuotedText] "{" (Lane)* "}"
Lane            := "{" Step* "}"                      // unlabeled parallel lane
GotoStep        := "goto" [Target] ["return" ("end" | "here")]
                   Target := FilePath "#" FlowId      // other file (workspace-relative)
                          | FlowId                    // same file
InfoStep        := "info" QuotedText
ConclusionStep  := "conclusion" QuotedText
```

Rules:

* **MsgStep resolution**: the `(from,to)` pair (direction-insensitive) must match ≥1
  existing link in the file (or via imports). `as RefId` disambiguates; `flip` plays the
  step reversed (e.g. a response) without altering the underlying link.
* `alt` branches are OR; playback offers a chooser (default = first branch; choice is a
  playback-time concern, never stored).
* `par` lanes animate concurrently; visual lane split during those beats.
* `goto` may cross files (imports not required for goto — navigation-only); `return end`
  resumes after the goto step, `return here` at the goto step (default `end`).
* Empty flow, or flow whose every step is unreachable (no intro/msg/process), is a
  validation warning.

Example (see SPEC §7 for semantics):

```
flow "Happy path" as happy {
  intro "Customer buys a cart"
  user -> shop : "adds to cart"
  process api "Validates cart"
  alt "payment method" {
    "card"    { api -requests-> psp : "charge" }
    "invoice" { api -requests-> inv : "create invoice" }
  }
  par {
    { api -publishes-> events }
    { api -requests-> mail : "receipt" }
  }
  info "PCI scope ends at PSP"
  goto refunds
  conclusion "Order stored"
}
```

## 7. Views, positions, styles

### 7.1 Views

```
ViewStmt := "view" QuotedName ["as" Id] "{" ViewLine* "}"
ViewLine := "layout" ("auto" Dir | "saved")
          | "hide" "tag" Ident                       // repeatable
          | "hide" Id                                 // repeatable (element-level)
          | "position" Id "(" Number "," Number ")"   // saved coords, canvas units
          | "pin" Id                                  // excluded from auto-layout
```

* A file with no `view` gets the implicit default view (auto layout, everything visible).
* `layout saved` uses the `position` lines; nodes without position are auto-placed.
* Camera state (zoom/scroll) is **never persisted** in PDL (session concern).

### 7.2 Coordinates

Canvas units: 1 = 1 px at 100% zoom; origin top-left; y grows downward. Auto-layout
(dagre) outputs are written back only when the user explicitly commits layout ("apply
layout to file") — never silently.

### 7.3 Style overrides

```
style Id "{" StyleLine* "}"
StyleLine := fill ColorHex | stroke ColorHex | text ColorHex | icon Ident
           | shape (rect | round | cyl | queue | person | note)
```

* Colors: `#rgb` / `#rrggbb`. Theme supplies all defaults; `style` is override-only.
* Style overrides are also valid **inside** object/link blocks (`style { … }` line),
  canonical printer hoists them to top-level `style` statements? **No** — printer keeps
  styles where the user put them (stable diffing); hoisting is a formatter option, off
  by default.

## 8. Mermaid import (converter)

Input: `flowchart`/`graph` (mermaid v10 subset) and C4 statements. Converter = pure
function `text → PDL` (+ diagnostics), implemented identically in TS and Go (IR parity,
SPEC §8.2).

**Shape → kind mapping** (documented heuristic; overridable via `--map` flag on
`panelcraft convert`):

| Mermaid shape | PDL kind |
|---|---|
| `id(text)` rounded | component |
| `id[text]` rect | container (level container) / system (level context) |
| `id([text])` stadium | system_ext |
| `id[(text)]` cylinder | datastore |
| `id((text))` circle | person |
| `id>text]` asymmetric | queue |
| `id{text}` rhombus | note (decision) |
| `subgraph` | group (children → `contains`) |

**C4 mapping**: `System(x,…)`→system, `System_Ext`→system_ext, `Person`→person,
`Container*`→container, `Component*`→component, `SystemDb/Queue`→datastore/queue,
`Rel(a,b,"label","tech")`→link (`tech` → link `style` comment property `technology`).
`Show*`, `Update*`, layout/skinparams: ignored with info diagnostics.

Edges: `-->`, `---`, `-.->`, `==>`, labels (`|text|` and `--text-->`), chained
`a --> b --> c` (expanded), `&` multi-endpoints (expanded to pairs).

Everything else (classes, themes, flowcharts-v2 specifics like `&` subgraph links,
nested subgraph ids): warning + skipped, never silent.

## 9. Mermaid export (lossy, declared)

`PDL → flowchart TD` with:

* Objects → shapes per inverse mapping table; groups → `subgraph`.
* Links → `-->` with `|label|`; type retained in label prefix when non-`uses`
  (`"requests: POST /checkout"`) — cheap, lossless-enough convention.
* Tags → mermaid `classDef` (one class per tag), applied via `class` statements.
* Fill colors of `style` overrides → `style id fill:#…`.

**Dropped (declared, per SPEC FR-M4):** flows, positions/layout, views, imports
(exported file is flattened: imported objects inlined and marked via comment `%%
imported from …`), properties, notes detach, icons, waypoints, custom shapes.
C4 export mode (`--c4`): emits C4Context/Container statements when kinds fit, else
fallback flowchart.

## 10. Validation rules (semantic pass; `panelcraft validate`)

| Code | Severity | Rule |
|---|---|---|
| P100 | error | duplicate object/flow/view id |
| P101 | error | link/flow-step endpoint resolves to nothing |
| P102 | error | import cycle |
| P103 | error | import path escapes workspace |
| P104 | error | flow msg-step references non-existent link pair (without `as`) |
| P105 | error | group `contains` unknown id / nested group in group (v1: flat groups) |
| P106 | error | note `attach` unknown id |
| P200 | warning | missing import file (renderable without it) |
| P201 | warning | orphan object (no links, no flow references) |
| P202 | warning | empty flow / flow without visual steps |
| P203 | warning | `style` targets non-existent id |
| P204 | info | position overlaps (view-time concern; reported, not fixed) |

Exit codes per SPEC FR-X. All findings carry `line:col` of the offending token.

## 11. Canonical formatting (printer)

* Fixed section order (§2), objects in **first-definition order**, links likewise.
* One attribute per line; 2-space indent per block level.
* Quotes on all strings; explicit link ids only when referenced (§4 rule).
* Printer is idempotent: `format(format(x)) == format(x)` — golden-tested.
* Formatter preserves comments by attaching them to the following statement.

## 12. Forward compatibility policy

* Unknown top-level statement: parse error (fail fast — version gate protects).
* Unknown *attribute* inside a known block: kept as raw data (`attributes[]` in IR),
  warning P2xx, re-emitted verbatim on print. Minor version bumps add attributes.
* Format minor version (`pcd 1.x`): additive only; `pcd 2` = new major, converter path.

## 13. EBNF (core, informative)

```ebnf
file        = "pcd" version , { stmt } ;
version     = number , [ "." number ] ;
stmt        = meta | import | object | link | flow | view | style ;
meta        = ("title" string) | ("level" ident) | ("direction" ident) | ("theme" ident) ;
import      = "import" ident "as" path ;
object      = kind ident , [ string ] , [ "{" , { attr } , "}" ] ;
attr        = ("description" , string) | ("technology" , string) | ("tag" , ident { ident })
            | ("property" , ident , string) | ("contains" , ident { ident })
            | ("attach" , ident) | ("icon" , ident) ;
link        = ident , arrow , ident , [ ":" , string ] , [ "as" , ident ] , [ linkblock ] ;
arrow       = [ "<" ] , "-" , [ ident , "-" ] , [ ">" ] ;   (* <-, ->, <->, -type-> *)
flow        = "flow" , [ string ] , [ "as" , ident ] , "{" , { step } , "}" ;
step        = intro | msg | process | alt | par | goto | info | conclusion ;
alt         = "alt" , [ string ] , "{" , { branch } , "}" ;
branch      = string , "{" , { step } , "}" ;
par         = "par" , [ string ] , "{" , { lane } , "}" ;
lane        = "{" , { step } , "}" ;
goto        = "goto" , [ path , "#" ] , ident , [ "return" , ("end"|"here") ] ;
view        = "view" , string , [ "as" , ident ] , "{" , { viewline } , "}" ;
style       = "style" , ident , "{" , { styleline } , "}" ;
```

(Formal EBNF is the implementation reference; this section is the readable summary.
Where prose and EBNF disagree, prose wins until M1 lands and this doc is regenerated
from the grammar tests.)

---

## 14. Full example (normative sample, corpus seed `corpus/checkout.pcd`)

```
pcd 1.0
title "Checkout"
level container
direction LR

import common as "../common/actors.pcd"      # provides common.psp

person user "Shopper"
system shop "Webshop" {
  description "Storefront SPA"
  technology "React"
  tag core
  property owner "team-commerce"
}
container api "Checkout API" { technology "Go" tag core pci }
datastore db "Orders DB" { technology "PostgreSQL" }
queue events "order.events" { technology "Kafka" }
system_ext psp "Payment Provider"            # imported in real files; inlined here
group ctx "Checkout context" { contains api db }

user -> shop : "browses catalog"
shop -requests-> api : "POST /checkout" as L1
api -writes-> db
api -publishes-> events as L3
api -requests-> psp : "charge card" as L4

flow "Happy path" as happy {
  intro "Customer buys a cart"
  user -> shop : "adds to cart"
  process api "Validates cart"
  alt "payment method" {
    "card"    { api -> psp as L4 : "charge" }
    "invoice" { info "invoicing not in this story" }
  }
  par "fan-out" {
    { api -> events as L3 : "order created" }
    { process mail? "send receipt" }        # ← invalid id → P101 (kept for corpus test)
  }
  info "PCI scope ends at PSP"
  conclusion "Order stored"
}

view "Main" {
  layout auto LR
  position user (80, 120)
  position api (420, 90)
}

style api { fill #2d6cdf }
```

> The deliberately broken line (`mail?`) documents that validation reports P101 with
> position, while the rest of the file still parses — error isolation requirement.

{"content":"# agents.md — PanelCraft

Agentic development conventions for this repository. **Humans:** this file is also for
you — it is the contributor handbook in condensed form. Full product spec:
[docs/SPEC.md](docs/SPEC.md). Format spec: [docs/FILE-FORMAT.md](docs/FILE-FORMAT.md).

## Project in one paragraph

Client-only web app for IcePanel-style architecture diagrams (IcePanel = inspiration
only, no links/affiliation in docs): WYSIWYG SVG canvas + always-visible code view,
native `.pcd` format (own grammar, mermaid-inspired), mermaid import/export converters,
flows/animation, multi-file workspace in browser storage only (nothing server-side),
ZIP import/export, GitHub Pages hostable, single Go binary (serve + validate/convert/
render CLI). License **GPL-3.0-only**.

## Ground rules (non-negotiable)

1. **License**: every new source file starts with the GPL-3.0 SPDX header
   (`// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only`). Deps must be GPL-compatible
   (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD); new dependency ⇒ ADR first.
2. **Milestones are the contract** (SPEC §9). New ideas → backlog (SPEC §12), never
   silently expanded scope.
3. **Quality gates** (SPEC §8): Go `staticcheck` + `gocyclo ≤10/15`; TS `eslint`
   complexity ≤12, `tsc --noEmit` clean; **coverage ≥80% on core packages** (vitest
   thresholds enforce); corpus parity TS⇄Go is a CI gate.
4. **No unverified claims**: every "done" statement cites the command that proves it
   (test run, e2e pass, screenshot review). Mark unverified work as such.
5. **Storage stays browser-local.** Any change that adds a network call (beyond static
   asset load) violates SPEC FR-S1/N7 — reject in review. E2E no-network test is the
   enforcement.
6. **Docs stay human-readable.** agents.md and docs/ are written for people first;
   agent-optimized pointers secondary. No IcePanel URLs in docs (name-as-inspiration
   only).

## Commands

```bash
# web
npm ci                       # install (lockfile committed)
npm run dev                  # vite dev server :5173
npm run check                # tsc + eslint (CI gate)
npm test                     # vitest run + coverage thresholds
npm run e2e                  # playwright (build first: npm run build)
npm run build                # static bundle → web/dist

# go
go build ./...               # bin: panelcraft (embeds web/dist — build web first)
go test ./...                # unit + corpus parity
go vet ./... && staticcheck ./...
gocyclo -over 15 . && echo OK   # CI fails >15; target ≤10

# cli smoke
panelcraft validate testdata/corpus
panelcraft convert testdata/corpus/checkout.pcd -o /tmp/x.pcd
panelcraft serve --addr :8080 --open
```

## Definition of done (per task)

- [ ] Real check run and pasted as evidence (not "should pass")
- [ ] Coverage gate green for touched packages
- [ ] Complexity gates green (no new `// rationale:` exceptions without ADR)
- [ ] E2E scenario green if UI-touching; screenshots captured
- [ ] **Vision review pass if UI-touching**: screenshots reviewed against
      docs/STYLE-GUIDE.md checklist; defects filed or fixed (SPEC §8.4)
- [ ] Docs updated (SPEC/FILE-FORMAT/ARCHITECTURE/CHANGELOG as applicable)
- [ ] GPL headers present on new files

## Working conventions

* **Small diffs, one concern per change.** No opportunistic cleanup, no drive-by
  reformatting.
* **SOLID**: engine packages depend on interfaces (ports), not concrete impls
  (LayoutEngine, Storage, Clock, AnimPlayer are ports). See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
* **Parser changes**: touch `engine/format` + golden corpus in the same change; run
  parity both sides before pushing. Never hand-edit `*.ir.json` goldens — regenerate
  via `npm run corpus:accept` / `go run ./internal/corpus -accept` and diff-review.
* **Tests**: unit-test the failing behavior first (test-first for bugfixes); no test
  weakening to get green; flaky test = fix root cause, no retries/skips.
* **Commits**: imperative subject ≤72 chars, body explains *why*; reference FR-/SPEC-§.
* **Branches**: `feat/<milestone>-<slug>`, PRs into `main`; CI must be green before
  merge (no direct pushes to main).

## E2E + vision loop (UI work)

1. Implement → `npm run build` → `npm run e2e` (Playwright chromium).
2. Screenshot baselines land in `e2e/__screenshots__/`; review diffs deliberately.
3. Open the app (dev server or built dist) via browser automation; capture milestone
   screenshots (light+dark).
4. Review screenshots vs STYLE-GUIDE checklist (alignment, contrast, spacing, empty
   states, animation end states). File defects with screenshot refs; fix; re-shoot.
5. Record review outcome in milestone log (docs/milestones/M< n >.md).

## Repo map (who owns what)

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `web/src/engine/format` | PDL parser/printer, mermaid converters (TS) |
| `web/src/engine/model` | IR types + operations, validation |
| `web/src/engine/{render,layout,flows,anim}` | SVG engine, dagre port, step machine |
| `web/src/workspace` | virtual FS, ZIP, IDB store, undo |
| `web/src/ui` | Preact components, panels, dialogs |
| `cmd/panelcraft` | Go CLI entry (serve/validate/convert/render) |
| `internal/{ir,pdl,server,render}` | Go IR codec, PDL parser, embedded server, chromedp render |
| `testdata/corpus` | golden .pcd + .ir.json (shared TS/Go) |
| `e2e` | Playwright specs + screenshots |
| `docs` | SPEC, FILE-FORMAT, ARCHITECTURE, STYLE-GUIDE, milestones, adr/ |

## When stuck (debug protocol)

1. Reproduce with the smallest failing command/test; state exact output.
2. One hypothesis at a time; instrument, don't speculate-edit.
3. Two failed fix attempts on the same bug ⇒ stop, write up findings
   (attempts + evidence), top-2 hypotheses + discriminating test, ask for review.
4. Never weaken tests, never hard-code around failures you haven't explained.

{"content":"# ADR-0001: Custom SVG rendering engine (no mermaid.js in the editor)

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2025-11-07
- Context: SPEC D2

## Context

IcePanel-class features — live WYSIWYG editing (drag, resize, inline link creation),
per-step flow animation with camera moves and dimming, tag fading, ghosted imported
objects — require imperative control over the scene graph and animation timeline.

## Options considered

1. **Render with mermaid.js** — faithful mermaid look, zero renderer code.
   Rejected: SVG output is opaque (no stable per-element handles), no editing
   interaction model, animation limited to CSS poking at generated markup; would
   force a "preview-only" mermaid pane and a second editor paradigm. Two paradigms
   = two bugs per feature.
2. **Adopt a graph library (Cytoscape.js / maxGraph / x6)** — faster start for
   pan/zoom/hit-testing. Rejected as core: heavyweight abstractions we'd fight
   (custom data model in, custom serialization out), styling/animation control
   still partial; library churn risk. (Kept as fallback if custom engine blows the
   N1 perf budget — decision point M2.)
3. **Custom SVG engine** — chosen.

## Decision

Build a framework-agnostic TypeScript SVG engine: scene-graph model → SVG DOM,
layers (edges/objects/overlay/animation), hit-testing, viewport transform, WAAPI/
CSS-driven animation. Preact renders UI chrome *around* the canvas, never inside it.

## Consequences

+ Full control of animation, dimming, ghosting, camera; no abstraction fights.
+ Engine packages are plain TS → fast unit tests, no DOM framework coupling.
− We own pan/zoom, hit-testing, edge routing quality (orthogonal routing is the
  hard 20%) — mitigated by dagre for auto-layout (ADR-0004) and perf budget N1.
− Milestone M2 grows; accepted consciously.
","path":"docs/adr/0001-custom-svg-engine.md"}

{"content":"# ADR-0002: Native `.pcd` grammar (mermaid-inspired, not mermaid-compatible)

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2025-11-07
- Context: SPEC D7, FR-M6

## Context

The format must express things mermaid cannot: flows with 8 step types (alt/par/
goto nesting), typed links, per-object properties, imports, saved views/positions,
style overrides. Product owner ruled: mermaid *compatibility* is not required;
grammar may be mermaid-*inspired*; import/export converters provide interop
(import: lossless on supported subset; export: declared feature drop).

## Options considered

1. **Mermaid + extension comment block** (`%% pcd:begin … %% pcd:end`) — keeps files
   renderable by mermaid tools. Rejected: two syntaxes in one file (line grammar +
   YAML-in-comments), fragile tooling story, escaped the "code view is the source of
   truth" goal — the extension block becomes a config dump, not readable source.
2. **YAML/JSON-native** — trivial parsing, but hostile as a *hand-edited* code view
   (noise-to-signal for diagrams; arrow semantics lost).
3. **Own line-oriented grammar, mermaid-flavored** — chosen: arrows/labels feel
   familiar, blocks (`flow`, `view`, `group`) model our semantics directly.

## Decision

PDL `pcd/1` as specified in docs/FILE-FORMAT.md: `pcd 1.0` magic header, typed
object statements, typed arrow links (`a -requests-> b : "label" as L1`), nested
flow blocks, view/position/style sections. Mermaid enters/leaves only via the
converters (import §8, export §9 of FILE-FORMAT.md).

## Consequences

+ One coherent syntax; flows/views/imports are first-class and readable.
+ Round-trip and canonical printing are fully under our control (golden corpus).
− No free "renders anywhere" property; mitigated by the always-available lossy
  mermaid export (FR-M4) and PNG/SVG export.
− Converter fidelity is a permanent maintenance surface — bounded by documented
  mapping tables + diagnostics (FR-M5) and shared corpus tests.
","path":"docs/adr/0002-native-pdl-grammar.md"}

{"content":"# ADR-0003: Browser-only persistence model

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2025-11-07
- Context: SPEC FR-S*, FR-H1, N7

## Context

Hard product constraint: **nothing server-side**. The app must survive reloads
(durable-enough local storage), support multi-file workspaces, and remain fully
functional on GitHub Pages *and* behind the Go binary with zero backend endpoints.

## Decision

* Persistence = **IndexedDB** (workspace blob + settings + snapshots), autosave
  debounced 800 ms; schema-versioned with forward-only migrations (FR-S5).
* Ephemeral mode (FR-S2) = in-memory only, explicit user opt-in, export reminders.
* Quota errors degrade to ephemeral + warning (FR-S3). Clear-all-data = typed
  confirmation (FR-S4).
* The Go server exposes **read-only static + optional read-only `/files/*`** —
  no write endpoints by design; write-path absence is the guarantee.

## Alternatives considered

* localStorage only — 5 MB cap, synchronous, no blobs; rejected for workspace ZIPs.
* File System Access API as primary — powerful but Chromium-only and permission
  prompts hurt first-run UX; deferred to backlog (SPEC §12) as an *optional* mirror.
* OPFS — blob-friendly but same origin-partitioning caveats; IDB is more portable.

## Consequences

+ Truly static hosting; privacy provable in E2E (network-blocked suite green).
− "Clear browser data" loses work ⇒ ZIP export reminders + snapshots (FR-W7) are
  product answers, not optional polish.
− IDB availability in private-mode Safari quirks ⇒ wrapper layer with in-memory
  fallback, unit-tested via fake-indexeddb.
","path":"docs/adr/0003-browser-only-storage.md"}

{"content":"# ADR-0004: Dependency policy and the allowed set

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2025-11-07
- Context: constraint "minimal external dependencies; stdlib first; libraries allowed
  when they remove extreme complexity"

## Policy

1. Default = platform standard library (browser or Go std). A dependency needs a
   written reason: complexity avoided, correctness risk reduced, spec compliance.
2. Runtime (ships to users) deps are held to a stricter bar than dev/build/test deps.
3. Every new dependency: ADR + license compatibility check (GPL-3.0-compatible:
   MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD) + bundle-size note. No transitive-surprise rule: lockfile diff
   reviewed in the same PR.
4. Re-evaluate at M7: anything replaceable by ~100 lines of owned code gets replaced.

## Approved runtime set (v1)

| Dependency | Why | Alternative rejected |
|---|---|---|
| preact (+ htm via jsx runtime) | UI chrome: panels, trees, dialogs — state wiring by hand would dominate complexity | vanilla custom vdom (slow, risky); react (heavier) |
| codemirror 6 | code view: incremental parse, diagnostics gutters, performs on big files | textarea + highlighting lib (no gutter/diag model) |
| dagre | layered auto-layout (N1); hand-rolling Sugiyama = high-risk algorithm code | own Sugiyama (post-v1 candidate); ELK (wasm, heavy) |
| chromedp (Go) | headless render CLI via CDP; pure Go, no cgo | os/exec chrome --screenshot (no settle control) |
| fflate *(conditional)* | ZIP fallback **only** when `CompressionStream`/`DecompressionStream` unavailable (Safari <16.4); loaded lazily | always-on zip lib (violates stdlib-first) |

ZIP base path = `CompressionStream`/`DecompressionStream` + thin container code
(owned, unit-tested) — stdlib-first honored; fflate is the documented fallback, not
the default.

## Approved dev/test set

vite, typescript, eslint(+ts), vitest(+fake-indexeddb, jsdom),
@testing-library/preact, playwright(+pixelmatch), staticcheck, gocyclo/gocognit.

## Explicit non-dependencies (v1)

React, state libs (redux/zustand), CSS frameworks (tailwind — hand-rolled design
tokens instead), chart/graph engines (cytoscape/x6), yaml libs (PDL parser is
hand-written), mermaid.js.
","path":"docs/adr/0004-dependency-policy.md"}

{"content":"# ADR-0005: Licensing — GPL-3.0-only

- Status: Accepted
- Date: 2025-11-07
- Context: product owner decision

## Decision

PanelCraft is licensed under the **GNU General Public License v3.0 only**
(SPDX: `GPL-3.0-only`).

## Implementation rules

1. `LICENSE` (canonical GPLv3 text) at repo root — added in M0 scaffolding.
2. Every source file carries `SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only` (+ standard GPL
   header comment in Go/TS files).
3. **Dependency gate**: only GPL-compatible licenses (MIT, Apache-2.0, BSD, ISC).
   License check recorded in the ADR proposing each new dependency (see ADR-0004).
   Approved today: preact (MIT), codemirror (MIT), dagre (MIT), chromedp (Apache-2.0),
   fflate (MIT); dev tools MIT/Apache-2.0 — all compatible.
4. **Binary distribution** (GitHub Releases, SPEC FR-H2): corresponding source is
   satisfied by linking the public repository; release notes cite the exact commit.
5. **Documentation**: repo docs ship under the project license; CC-BY-SA-4.0 is the
   approved alternative for `docs/` and sample diagrams if stricter attribution is
   later desired (dual-declaration at file top).
6. GitHub Pages serves unmodified GPL-licensed assets — distribution is plain
   conveyance; no additional terms may be imposed (GPL §7).

## Consequences

+ Strong copyleft protects the project against closed forks.
− Blocks Apache-2.0-only or GPL-incompatible dependencies (e.g. some CC
  non-commercial assets) — the ADR dependency gate enforces this early.
− Icon fonts/clipart must be license-checked (GPL-compatible or public-domain) —
  tracked in M5 (icons milestone).
","path":"docs/adr/0005-gpl-licensing.md"}

# agents.md — PanelCraft

Agentic development conventions for this repository. **Humans:** this file is also for
you — it is the contributor handbook in condensed form. Full product spec:
[docs/SPEC.md](docs/SPEC.md). Format spec: [docs/FILE-FORMAT.md](docs/FILE-FORMAT.md).

## Project in one paragraph

Client-only web app for IcePanel-style architecture diagrams (IcePanel = inspiration
only, no links/affiliation in docs): WYSIWYG SVG canvas + always-visible code view,
native `.pcd` format (own grammar, mermaid-inspired), mermaid import/export converters,
flows/animation, multi-file workspace in browser storage only (nothing server-side),
ZIP import/export, GitHub Pages hostable, single Go binary (serve + validate/convert/
render CLI). License **GPL-3.0-only**.

## Ground rules (non-negotiable)

1. **License**: every new source file starts with the GPL-3.0 SPDX header
   (`// SPDX-License-Identifier: GPL-3.0-only`). Deps must be GPL-compatible
   (MIT/Apache-2.0/BSD); new dependency ⇒ ADR first.
2. **Milestones are the contract** (SPEC §9). New ideas → backlog (SPEC §12), never
   silently expanded scope.
3. **Quality gates** (SPEC §8): Go `staticcheck` + `gocyclo ≤10/15`; TS `eslint`
   complexity ≤12, `tsc --noEmit` clean; **coverage ≥80% on core packages** (vitest
   thresholds enforce); corpus parity TS⇄Go is a CI gate.
4. **No unverified claims**: every "done" statement cites the command that proves it
   (test run, e2e pass, screenshot review). Mark unverified work as such.
5. **Storage stays browser-local.** Any change that adds a network call (beyond static
   asset load) violates SPEC FR-S1/N7 — reject in review. E2E no-network test is the
   enforcement.
6. **Docs stay human-readable.** agents.md and docs/ are written for people first;
   agent-optimized pointers secondary. No IcePanel URLs in docs (name-as-inspiration
   only).

## Commands

```bash
# web
npm ci                       # install (lockfile committed)
npm run dev                  # vite dev server :5173
npm run check                # tsc + eslint (CI gate)
npm test                     # vitest run + coverage thresholds
npm run e2e                  # playwright (build first: npm run build)
npm run build                # static bundle → web/dist

# go
go build ./...               # bin: panelcraft (embeds web/dist — build web first)
go test ./...                # unit + corpus parity
go vet ./... && staticcheck ./...
gocyclo -over 15 . && echo OK   # CI fails >15; target ≤10

# cli smoke
panelcraft validate testdata/corpus
panelcraft convert testdata/corpus/checkout.pcd -o /tmp/x.pcd
panelcraft serve --addr :8080 --open
```

## Definition of done (per task)

- [ ] Real check run and pasted as evidence (not "should pass")
- [ ] Coverage gate green for touched packages
- [ ] Complexity gates green (no new `// rationale:` exceptions without ADR)
- [ ] E2E scenario green if UI-touching; screenshots captured
- [ ] **Vision review pass if UI-touching**: screenshots reviewed against
      docs/STYLE-GUIDE.md checklist; defects filed or fixed (SPEC §8.4)
- [ ] Docs updated (SPEC/FILE-FORMAT/ARCHITECTURE/CHANGELOG as applicable)
- [ ] GPL headers present on new files

## Working conventions

* **Small diffs, one concern per change.** No opportunistic cleanup, no drive-by
  reformatting.
* **SOLID**: engine packages depend on interfaces (ports), not concrete impls
  (LayoutEngine, Storage, Clock, AnimPlayer are ports). See docs/ARCHITECTURE.md.
* **Parser changes**: touch `engine/format` + golden corpus in the same change; run
  parity both sides before pushing. Never hand-edit `*.ir.json` goldens — regenerate
  via `npm run corpus:accept` / `go run ./internal/corpus -accept` and diff-review.
* **Tests**: unit-test the failing behavior first (test-first for bugfixes); no test
  weakening to get green; flaky test = fix root cause, no retries/skips.
* **Commits**: imperative subject ≤72 chars, body explains *why*; reference FR-/SPEC-§.
* **Branches**: `feat/<milestone>-<slug>`, PRs into `main`; CI must be green before
  merge (no direct pushes to main).

## E2E + vision loop (UI work)

1. Implement → `npm run build` → `npm run e2e` (Playwright chromium).
2. Screenshot baselines land in `e2e/__screenshots__/`; review diffs deliberately.
3. Open the app (dev server or built dist) via browser automation; capture milestone
   screenshots (light+dark).
4. Review screenshots vs STYLE-GUIDE checklist (alignment, contrast, spacing, empty
   states, animation end states). File defects with screenshot refs; fix; re-shoot.
5. Record review outcome in milestone log (docs/milestones/M< n >.md).

## Repo map (who owns what)

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| `web/src/engine/format` | PDL parser/printer, mermaid converters (TS) |
| `web/src/engine/model` | IR types + operations, validation |
| `web/src/engine/{render,layout,flows,anim}` | SVG engine, dagre port, step machine |
| `web/src/workspace` | virtual FS, ZIP, IDB store, undo |
| `web/src/ui` | Preact components, panels, dialogs |
| `cmd/panelcraft` | Go CLI entry (serve/validate/convert/render) |
| `internal/{ir,pdl,server,render}` | Go IR codec, PDL parser, embedded server, chromedp render |
| `testdata/corpus` | golden .pcd + .ir.json (shared TS/Go) |
| `e2e` | Playwright specs + screenshots |
| `docs` | SPEC, FILE-FORMAT, ARCHITECTURE, STYLE-GUIDE, milestones, adr/ |

## When stuck (debug protocol)

1. Reproduce with the smallest failing command/test; state exact output.
2. One hypothesis at a time; instrument, don't speculate-edit.
3. Two failed fix attempts on the same bug ⇒ stop, write up findings
   (attempts + evidence), top-2 hypotheses + discriminating test, ask for review.
4. Never weaken tests, never hard-code around failures you haven't explained.

-## 1. Summary
-
-PanelCraft is a client-only web application for creating, editing, animating and sharing
-software architecture diagrams, inspired by IcePanel (inspiration only — no affiliation,
-no links in documentation):
-
-* **WYSIWYG canvas editor** — drop components, draw typed connections, edit properties inline.
-* **Code view** — the diagram source is always visible, editable and the single source of
-  truth; canvas ⇄ code stay synchronized (mermaid-flavored text format with extensions).
-* **Mermaid interop** — imports mermaid `flowchart` and C4 diagrams via converter;
-  exports to mermaid with declared feature drop. The native grammar is its own —
-  *inspired by* mermaid, not bound to its syntax.
-* **Flows & animation** — IcePanel-style step-by-step flow playback (8 step types) over
-  static diagrams.
-* **Workspace** — multiple files, directory tree, per-file import/export, full ZIP
-  export/import.
-* **Zero server storage** — everything lives in the browser; nothing is sent anywhere.
-* **Shipable two ways** — fully static on GitHub Pages, *and* as a single Go binary
-  (Windows/Linux/macOS) that serves the app plus a headless CLI (`validate` / `convert`
-  / `render`).
-
-### Out of scope (explicitly)
-
-Real-time collaboration, authentication, server-side persistence, AI assistance, mobile
-native apps. Full mermaid feature coverage (only the subset in [FILE-FORMAT.md](FILE-FORMAT.md)).
-
----
-
-## 2. Decisions locked with product owner
-
-| # | Decision | Choice |
-|---|----------|--------|
-| D1 | Model topology | **Hybrid**: files are standalone diagrams; objects may reference other files via `imports` (link-style reuse) |
-| D2 | Rendering | **Custom SVG engine**; mermaid.js is *never* the editor renderer — mermaid is import/export text format only |
-| D3 | Go binary role | Static app server **+ headless CLI** (`validate`, `convert`, `render` via headless Chrome) |
-| D4 | Frontend stack | **Preact** for UI chrome + framework-agnostic TypeScript SVG engine |
-| D5 | Flows | **All 8 IcePanel step types in v1** (see §7) |
-| D6 | Quality gates | Go: `staticcheck` + `gocyclo`; JS: `eslint` (incl. complexity rules) + `vitest`, **≥80% coverage on core packages**; E2E: **Playwright + vision review in dev loop** |
-| D7 | Native file format | Own `.pcd` grammar, mermaid-**inspired**; **no mermaid-validity requirement**. Mermaid handled by import converter and lossy exporter only |
-| D8 | License | **GPL-3.0-only** (SPDX `GPL-3.0-only`), LICENSE file at repo root |
-
-Rationale for each: ADR 0001–0005.
-

-
-## 3. Users & key scenarios
-
-**Persona A — Architect (author).** Maintains a workspace of diagrams describing a
-system landscape. Creates diagrams visually, refines them in code view, animates flows
-to explain request journeys.
-
-**Persona B — Reviewer (reader).** Opens a shared `.pcd` file or ZIP, walks flows in
-play mode, exports PNG/SVG for docs.
-
-**Top scenarios (must work end-to-end):**
-
-1. *S1 Create*: new file → drag person/system/container onto canvas → link them → set
-   properties → diagram renders live; code view shows updated source.
-2. *S2 Code round-trip*: paste a mermaid `C4Container` snippet into code view → canvas
-   renders it → edit node in canvas → code view updates; file remains valid mermaid
-   (PanelCraft extensions live in comment block).
-3. *S3 Flow playback*: define 6-step flow (incl. one `alt`, one `par`) → press Play →
-   camera focus + animated edges step-by-step; non-active elements dim.
-4. *S4 Workspace IO*: build directory tree `landscape/`, `systems/billing/` → export ZIP →
-   clear browser data → import ZIP → identical workspace.
-5. *S5 Mermaid import*: open `architecture.mmd` (flowchart + subgraphs) → converted to
-   `.pcd`, auto-laid-out, fully editable.
-6. *S6 CLI*: `panelcraft validate ./diagrams` lints all files (CI gate);
-   `panelcraft render checkout.pcd --out checkout.png` produces a PNG via headless Chrome.
-7. *S7 Static hosting*: open the GitHub Pages URL → full functionality offline-capable,
-   no backend calls (verified by network monitor in E2E).
-

-
-## 4. Functional requirements
-
-### 4.1 Workspace & files (FR-W)
-
-* **FR-W1** Virtual file tree with folders and `.pcd` files; create, rename, delete,
-  move (drag & drop), duplicate.
-* **FR-W2** Multi-tab editing; unsaved-changes indicator; autosave (see FR-S1).
-* **FR-W3** Per-file import: `.pcd`, `.mmd`/`.mermaid` (mermaid text), `.txt` (treated as mermaid).
-* **FR-W4** Per-file export: `.pcd`, `.mmd` (mermaid subset export), `.svg`, `.png`
-  (current view), `.seq.mmd` (flows exported as mermaid `sequenceDiagram`, optional M6).
-* **FR-W5** Workspace ZIP export (`workspace.zip`, plain folder layout + optional
-  `panelcraft.workspace.json` manifest) and ZIP import; round-trip must be lossless.
-* **FR-W6** Global quick search (`Ctrl/Cmd+P`): files, objects, flows (M6).
-* **FR-W7** Snapshots: manual named snapshots of the whole workspace, restore point
-  (M6, local only).
-
-### 4.2 Canvas editor (FR-C)
-
-* **FR-C1** Pan (space-drag / wheel-drag / trackpad), zoom (wheel/pinch, 10%–400%),
-  fit-to-selection, fit-to-diagram, zoom controls, mini-map (M6).
-* **FR-C2** Grid + snap-to-grid (toggleable); alignment guides when dragging.
-* **FR-C3** Stencil palette (C4 types): Person, Software System, External System,
-  Container, Component, Data Store, Queue/Topic, Group/Boundary, Note.
-  Drag-drop or click-to-place.
-* **FR-C4** Objects: select, multi-select (rubber band, shift-click), drag, resize
-  (groups/boundaries), rotate *not* supported (C4 shapes are axis-aligned).
-* **FR-C5** Inline rename (double-click), description tooltip, icon per object
-  (built-in icon set, M5).
-* **FR-C6** Properties panel: name, description, technology, tags (multi),
-  custom key-value properties, style overrides (fill, border, text color, icon).
-* **FR-C7** Connections: drag from port/edge halo to target; typed links
-  (`uses`, `includes`, `requests`, `returns`, `publishes`, `subscribes`, `reads`,
-  `writes`, `data`, custom); label; direction (uni/bi); arrowhead styles; dashed/solid.
-* **FR-C8** Edge routing: orthogonal (default), curved (bezier), straight; drag
-  waypoints; per-edge style override.
-* **FR-C9** Undo/redo (command stack, coalesced typing/drag operations, ≥100 steps),
-  full keyboard shortcuts (§10).
-* **FR-C10** Context menus: canvas, object, edge (duplicate, delete, bring-to-front,
-  add to group, create flow step from link…).
-* **FR-C11** Dependencies view of selected object: highlight incoming/outgoing + list
-  panel (M6).
-* **FR-C12** Copy/paste/duplicate objects within and across files (internal clipboard;
-  cross-file paste resolves missing imports by inlining).
-
-### 4.3 Code view (FR-K)
-
-* **FR-K1** Split layout: canvas + code side-by-side (horizontal or vertical), or
-  single-pane toggle. CodeMirror-based editor (see ADR-0004) with PanelCraft syntax
-  highlighting.
-* **FR-K2** Live two-way sync, debounced (canvas → code ≤150 ms; code → canvas on
-  idle/pause or explicit apply if parse errors).
-* **FR-K3** Diagnostics: parse/validation errors shown inline (line:col) + problem
-  panel; error state never loses user text.
-* **FR-K4** Format-on-save (canonical pretty-printer, idempotent).
-* **FR-K5** The saved file is the **source of truth**; canvas state is a projection.
-  Closing a file with diverged editor buffer prompts to apply/discard.
-
-### 4.4 Mermaid interop (FR-M) — details in FILE-FORMAT.md
-
-* **FR-M1** Import converter, mermaid `flowchart`/`graph` (incl. subgraphs, edge labels,
-  shapes) → PDL, with shape→semantic-type mapping (documented table) and auto-layout.
-* **FR-M2** Import converter, mermaid C4 (`C4Context`, `C4Container`, `C4Component`,
-  `C4Dynamic` incl. `System*`, `Container*`, `Rel*`, `Deployment*` subset) → PDL
-  objects/links; `Show*`/layout directives ignored.
-* **FR-M3** Import converter, mermaid `sequenceDiagram` → optional conversion to a Flow
-  over participant boxes (M6).
-* **FR-M4** Export to mermaid (`flowchart`): nodes, typed edges, labels, subgroups;
-  **feature drop is declared and documented** — flows/animations, manual positions
-  (replaced by auto-layout), styles (approximated by mermaid classes), properties,
-  imports are not representable. Export is one-way; PDL remains the only source of truth.
-* **FR-M5** Import diagnostics: unsupported mermaid constructs reported with line:col;
-  conversion never silently drops content. Export fidelity matrix documented (FR-M4).
-* **FR-M6** No mermaid-validity requirement on `.pcd` files; mermaid compatibility is
-  converter-only, in both directions.
-
-### 4.5 Flows & animation (FR-F)
-
-IcePanel-style visual storytelling over the static diagram.
-
-* **FR-F1** Multiple named flows per diagram; flow editor: ordered step list, drag to
-  reorder, per-step title + description.
-* **FR-F2** Step types (all in v1):
-  | Type | Meaning | Visual behavior |
-  |---|---|---|
-  | `intro` | Set the scene | Show all steps overview; no dimming |
-  | `msg` | Message A→B over existing link (direction may be flipped for the step) | Animated moving token along edge, step number badge, focus both ends |
-  | `process` | Single object does something | Pulse/emphasis on object + badge |
-  | `alt` | OR branches | Branch selector UI; plays chosen path; others dimmed |
-  | `par` | AND parallel | Steps animate concurrently on split lanes |
-  | `goto` | Jump to another flow (same or other file), optional return point | Navigate; breadcrumb to return |
-  | `info` | Free text not tied to elements | Info toast/card |
-  | `conclusion` | Close story | Show summary; un-dim |
-* **FR-F3** Play mode: play/pause/step-forward/step-back/restart, per-step auto delay
-  (default 2.5 s, configurable per step), exit restores pre-play view state.
-* **FR-F4** Animation style: edge token (circle) traveling with trailing dash animation,
-  object emphasis ring, non-participants dimmed to 25% opacity, smooth camera
-  (pan/zoom to step actors, 300 ms ease). All timing constants in theme config.
-* **FR-F5** Reduced-motion: respect `prefers-reduced-motion` → crossfade instead of
-  movement.
-* **FR-F6** Flow validation: steps reference existing objects/links; dangling refs are
-  errors (code view + validate CLI).
-
-### 4.6 Views, tags, layout (FR-V)
-
-* **FR-V1** Tags on objects/links; tag filter bar → fade non-matching (perspectives).
-* **FR-V2** Named views per diagram: element visibility set, tag filters, saved
-  positions, layout mode (`auto:LR|TB` or `saved`). Diagram has ≥1 view; default view
-  implicit.
-* **FR-V3** Auto-layout: layered (direction LR/TB) via dagre behind a `LayoutEngine`
-  port; deterministic for identical input (stable ordering by id).
-* **FR-V4** Manual positions stored in file; mixing auto + pinned nodes supported.
-
-### 4.7 Imports & reuse (FR-I) — hybrid model (D1)
-
-* **FR-I1** `imports:` section maps aliases → relative file paths; imported file's
-  *objects* are referenceable (ghost rendering: dashed border, "imported" badge).
-* **FR-I2** Imported objects are read-only in the importing file; click-through opens
-  source file (workspace-relative).
-* **FR-I3** Cycle detection: import graph must be acyclic (error otherwise).
-* **FR-I4** Missing import file → explicit problem marker, diagram still renders
-  non-imported content.
-
-### 4.8 Storage (FR-S)
-
-* **FR-S1** Persistence: IndexedDB autosave, debounced 800 ms; last-open workspace
-  restored on load. Storage model = **browser-local only**; "nothing server-side" is a
-  hard constraint (E2E asserts zero network calls after initial load).
-* **FR-S2** Ephemeral mode ("private tab" toggle): in-memory only, no IDB writes;
-  export reminder banner every 10 min.
-* **FR-S3** Quota handling: surface quota errors; graceful degradation to ephemeral
-  mode with warning; storage usage indicator in settings.
-* **FR-S4** Reset/clear-all-data with typed confirmation.
-* **FR-S5** Schema versioning of stored workspace (migrations forward-only).
-
-### 4.9 CLI (Go binary) (FR-X)
-
-Single static binary, no runtime deps, all assets embedded (`go:embed`).
-
-* `panelcraft serve [--addr :8080] [--open] [dir]` — serves the SPA at `/`, workspace
-  files under `[dir]` read-only at `/files/*` (optional convenience for demo assets).
-  SPA fallback to `index.html`. No write endpoints, ever.
-* `panelcraft validate <file|dir>... [--json]` — parse + semantic validation
-  (dangling refs, import cycles, flow refs, duplicate ids). Exit 0 clean; exit 1
-  findings; exit 2 usage/IO error. CI-friendly.
-* `panelcraft convert <in.mmd> [-o out.pcd]` — mermaid → PanelCraft canonical form.
-* `panelcraft render <file.pcd> --out out.png|svg [--width 1920] [--theme dark|light]
-  [--view NAME] [--chrome /path/to/chrome]` — headless render via Chrome DevTools
-  Protocol (chromedp, pure Go). Serve embedded app, drive it, screenshot/serialize SVG.
-  Fails with actionable error if no Chrome found.
-* `panelcraft version`.
-
-### 4.10 Hosting (FR-H)
-
-* **FR-H1** GitHub Pages deployment of the built SPA on `main` (Actions). App runs
-  100% static; base-path configurable at build time (`/panelcraft/`).
-* **FR-H2** GitHub Releases attach binaries: `panelcraft_{linux,darwin,windows}_{amd64,arm64}`
-  (+ checksums). Windows = `.zip`, others `.tar.gz`.
-

-
-## 5. Non-functional requirements
-
-| ID | Requirement | Target |
-|----|-------------|--------|
-| N1 | Render/interaction perf | 60 fps pan/zoom & drag ≤300 objects; ≤2 000 objects usable (layer virtualization) |
-| N2 | Open time | 100-object file → interactive < 300 ms (mid-range laptop) |
-| N3 | Parser perf | 10k-line file parses < 1 s |
-| N4 | Binary size | < 30 MB compressed |
-| N5 | Accessibility | WCAG 2.1 AA for UI chrome; canvas: full keyboard object nav, ARIA live narration in play mode; `prefers-reduced-motion` honored |
-| N6 | Security | Strict CSP (no inline script eval in app), exported SVG sanitized (no scripts/foreignObject from untrusted labels), CLI: path traversal guarded, no telemetry |
-| N7 | Privacy | Zero network calls at runtime (self-hosted fonts or system font stack); verifiable in E2E |
-| N8 | Offline | App shell + last workspace available offline (service worker, M7) |
-| N9 | Browser support | Evergreen Chrome/Edge/Firefox/Safari (last 2 versions); `CompressionStream` required (Safari ≥16.4), fallback dependency fflate if feature absent (ADR-0004) |
-| N10 | i18n | English v1; all strings centralized for later l10n |
-
-### Visual style targets (validated by vision review, §9)
-
-* Dark-first theme, high contrast, C4-ish shape language (soft rectangles, person
-  glyph), consistent 4 px spacing grid, subtle shadows, 150–300 ms transitions.
-* Style guide + golden screenshots per milestone (docs/STYLE-GUIDE.md in M0).
-

-
-## 6. File format (summary — full spec in FILE-FORMAT.md)
-
-* Native format **PDL (PanelCraft Diagram Language)**, extension `.pcd`, UTF-8,
-  **own grammar inspired by mermaid** — deliberately *not* required to be valid mermaid
-  (D7). One coherent syntax for structure *and* semantics: typed nodes, typed links,
-  plus first-class `flow`, `view`, `import`, `style`, `tag` directives — no comment-block
-  workarounds.
-* Mermaid enters/leaves the tool exclusively through converters:
-  * import: mermaid → PDL (lossless for supported subset, diagnostics otherwise);
-  * export: PDL → mermaid (lossy, declared feature drop).
-* Guarantees:
-  * PDL ⇄ internal IR ⇄ PDL is lossless (canonical round-trip, golden-tested).
-  * Parser accepts unknown-but-parseable constructs as data (forward compatibility),
-    reports them as warnings; semantic validation is a separate pass.
-* Internal **IR = language-neutral JSON schema** — shared contract between the TS
-  implementation and the Go CLI (parser parity tests, §8).
-
----
-
-## 7. Domain model (IR overview)
-
-```
-Workspace { schemaVersion, files[], settings }
-File      { path, meta, imports[], objects[], links[], groups[], flows[], views[] }
-Object    { id, kind(person|system|system_ext|container|component|datastore|queue|group|note),
-            name, description, technology, tags[], properties{}, style{}, importedFrom? }
-Link      { id, from, to, type, label, direction(uni|bi), style{}, waypoints[] }
-Flow      { id, title, description?, steps[] }
-Step      { id, type(intro|msg|process|alt|par|goto|info|conclusion), title?, description?,
-            payload (per type: from/to/linkRef | on | branches[](label,steps[]) | branches[](steps[]) |
-                     target{file?,flow,return} | text) }
-View      { id, name, layout(auto:LR|auto:TB|saved), positions{}, hiddenTags?, elements? }
-```
-
-Rules: ids are stable strings (`[a-z][a-z0-9_]*`, unique per file); link endpoints must
-resolve to objects or imported aliases; flows reference link ids for `msg` steps
-(mermaid-imported edges get auto ids `L1..Ln` recorded in `links:` so flows survive
-round-trips).
-
